candidates.name: Paycheck Nation (cost-of-living & economic-anxiety explainers)
candidates.niche: US household-economy explainers: layoffs, housing lock-in, grocery inflation, retirement shortfalls, Gen Z affordability — 'why your paycheck doesn't work anymore', one story per video, driven by fresh government/industry data
candidates.format: 10-15 min faceless data-documentary: AI narration over stock b-roll + original charts built from BLS/Challenger/Fed data; 2-3 uploads/week, news-adjacent but evergreen framing
candidates.why_now: Cost-of-living anxiety is the dominant US economic story of 2026 (record AI-attributed layoffs per Challenger, affordability crisis), and the exact template was just proven: Edwards Economics went from first upload on 2025-03-26 to 358,000 subs and 12.26M views in ~15.5 months (verified via YouTube API), publishing every ~2 days.

demand_evidence.title: Edwards Economics channel
demand_evidence.finding: 358,000 subs, 12,265,230 total views, 90 videos; oldest upload 2025-03-26 — i.e., the entire channel was built in under 16 months (YouTube API channels.list + playlistItems full pagination)
H1 2026: 443,604 announced US job cuts, second-highest Jan-Jun total since 2020; AI the leading stated reason 4 consecutive months (fact from search snippet; direct fetch returned 403)

competitor_scan.notes: THE attainability proof: <16 months old, 90 videos, recent uploads 11k-194k views each (API-verified). Faceless, AI/VO narration over stock footage.
Genre ceiling: 1.72M subs, 283.6M views, 314 videos (API). Weekly cadence leaves the 2-3x/week news-reactive lane open.
366k subs, 950 videos since 2020 (API); adjacent finance-news lane, shows near-daily solo cadence is viable at 35k-125k views/video.

candidates.monetization_notes: Finance/personal-economy is top-tier RPM territory — one industry blog puts faceless finance RPM at roughly $10-25 (Overseeros, C-grade snippet claim, unverified). Sponsor fit: budgeting apps, brokerages, job platforms, newsletters. Evergreen re-watch on affordability topics.
candidates.production_complexity: Moderate-low: each video is a research brief (BLS/Challenger/Fed/news data) + original script + charts + stock b-roll + AI narration. Fastest production cycle of the four candidates; solo creator can hit 2-3/week.
candidates.risks: Fast-follower influx (the Edwards template is visible to everyone); doom-fatigue if the economy improves; commodity stock-footage look requires strong data/charts to differentiate; some topics skirt 'controversial issues' ad suitability.
candidates.originality_defense: Every video is an original script synthesizing primary data (jobs reports, Fed data, earnings) with custom-built charts and analysis — no reused footage narratives. Clears YouTube's July 2025 'inauthentic content' policy (policy rename fact from C-grade blog snippets) because the value is the research and thesis, not compiled clips.

candidates.name: The White-Collar Recession (AI & the future of work, by the numbers)
candidates.niche: Data-driven breakdowns of AI's impact on jobs and industries: monthly jobs-report explainers, 'can AI actually do this job' industry autopsies, company-by-company AI restructuring stories, historical automation parallels
candidates.format: 12-18 min faceless explainer: AI narration + original data visualizations + archival/stock footage; anchored to recurring data drops (Challenger reports, BLS releases, big-company layoff announcements) for built-in search demand every month
candidates.why_now: AI has been the #1 stated reason for US job cuts for four consecutive months — a streak with no precedent in outplacement data — with 101,743 AI-attributed cuts YTD and tech absorbing ~31% of all H1 2026 layoffs (Challenger via search snippets). Viewing demand is verified across many channels, yet no faceless channel owns this beat — views are scattered across CNN, BBC, tech channels, and career coaches (inference from scan).

candidates.monetization_notes: Careers + business + AI = premium advertiser triangle (B2B SaaS, upskilling platforms, job boards, resume/interview tools). Strong sponsorship fit beyond AdSense; recurring monthly report videos build predictable search traffic.
candidates.production_complexity: Moderate: requires genuine data literacy (Challenger/BLS/earnings-call parsing) and careful sourcing, but the monthly data cadence hands you a content calendar. Solo-feasible at 1-2 videos/week with AI narration and chart-heavy visuals.
candidates.risks: Thesis risk: if the 'AI layoffs' narrative deflates (some coverage already questions attribution — e.g., BBC's 'What If We're Wrong About AI Layoffs?'), demand cools; mitigate by framing as broader future-of-work/labor-economics channel. Crowded midfield of career-coach commentary, though little rigorous faceless documentary treatment (inference).
candidates.originality_defense: Original analysis of primary labor data and corporate filings with custom visualizations; each video advances a researched thesis rather than aggregating news clips. Skeptical, evidence-first framing differentiates from AI-hype and AI-doom content farms.

candidates.name: Private Equity Autopsies (who really killed your favorite brand)
candidates.niche: Follow-the-money post-mortems of PE-destroyed companies: Red Lobster, Joann, TGI Fridays, Party City, Toys R Us, plus healthcare, nursing homes, vet clinics, local news, HVAC roll-ups — the mechanism (LBOs, sale-leasebacks, dividend recaps) as the recurring villain
candidates.format: 15-20 min faceless investigative documentary: AI narration, court/bankruptcy filings on screen, original financial timelines and diagrams of each deal structure; 1 video/week
candidates.why_now: The PE-killed-brands story is exploding into mainstream awareness in 2025-26: a CNBC explainer on PE behind Red Lobster/TGI Fridays bankruptcies drew 280k views, and Sen. Elizabeth Warren's May 2026 'How Private Equity Gutted Local Malls' video hit 964k views (both API-verified) — while the dedicated faceless-documentary treatment of the PE angle appears unowned; incumbents (Company Man, Bright Sun Films, MagnatesMedia) tell general rise-and-fall stories, not deal-mechanics stories (inference from scans).

candidates.monetization_notes: Business/finance documentary audience = high RPM; strong evergreen tail (bankruptcy stories keep getting searched for years). Sponsor fit: investing platforms, business tools, newsletters. Series/franchise structure ('Autopsy #14') aids bingeing and membership upsell.
candidates.production_complexity: Moderate-high: each episode needs real document research (bankruptcy dockets, PitchBook-style deal history via news coverage, court filings), but sources are public and the narrative template repeats. 1/week solo with AI narration + motion-graphic deal diagrams.
candidates.risks: Defamation care required — stick to filed/adjudicated facts and hedge causal claims; politically charged framing can polarize; giants could adopt the angle (mitigation: volume + niche depth across unglamorous sectors like nursing homes and vet clinics that giants skip).
candidates.originality_defense: Built on primary documents (bankruptcy filings, SEC filings, court records) with original deal-structure diagrams and financial timelines — analysis no compilation channel can replicate; each video makes an argued case, satisfying YouTube's authenticity/originality bar.

candidates.name: Modern Fraud Files (2020s financial crime case documentaries)
candidates.niche: Closed-case documentaries of recent financial crime: fintech collapses (Frank, Synapse-style), crypto scams and rug pulls, PPP/pandemic fraud, Ponzi schemes from DOJ/SEC actions, startup fraud (Nikola-style) — cases with indictments/convictions and public court records
candidates.format: 15-20 min faceless case-file documentary: AI narration, court documents and SEC complaints on screen, timeline graphics; 1 video/week, each case sourced from DOJ/SEC press releases (an effectively infinite, legally safe topic well)
candidates.why_now: Financial-crime storytelling demand is proven at every scale (CNBC's American Greed has run 200+ episodes; giants like Coffeezilla own breaking scandals), while the 2020s produced an unprecedented backlog of adjudicated fraud cases — crypto, PPP, fintech — that established channels haven't systematically covered; a 366k-sub channel gets 87k-93k views per fraud story right now (API-verified).

candidates.monetization_notes: True-crime x finance doubles the watch-time of crime with the RPM of finance (RPM claim C-grade). Strong sponsor fit: identity protection, VPNs, fraud-monitoring, investing tools — advertisers that specifically seek scam-aware audiences. Excellent evergreen back-catalog behavior.

candidates.risks: Coffeezilla and news channels own breaking scandals — must position as 'case closed' retrospectives, not investigations; defamation risk managed by covering only indicted/convicted cases; some ad-suitability sensitivity around crime content; audience overlap with true-crime is unproven for AI-narrated formats (inference).
candidates.originality_defense: Primary-document journalism: each script is original synthesis of court filings, SEC complaints, and reporting, with the creator's own case chronology and analysis — the opposite of reused-content compilation; visible document sourcing on screen also builds trust and demonetization resistance.
